title: The low basis theorem

based_on.title: Lecture notes in Computability Theory
based_on.pages: December 3, 2008 version; section 46, Proposition 46.5, p. 137; finite certificates and one fixed ordinary index compiler expanded

summary: Choose a path through any infinite computable binary tree while keeping its own oracle-halting problem at the ordinary halting degree.
abstract: A program may decide which finite binary words are allowed even when no program can produce an infinite sequence whose prefixes are all allowed. If allowed words form a tree with nodes at every length, the halting oracle can compute a path. Can one also keep halting for programs using that path no harder than ordinary halting? The low basis theorem says yes. Whenever any path exists, some path is low: its own halting problem has exactly the ordinary halting degree. We prove this by retaining divergence requirements whenever their finite restrictions leave a path possible. The theorem applies to every nonempty effectively closed collection of binary sequences and yields a noncomputable low binary function that avoids every defined program output on its own index.
